scope: Decoder-worker staging and deferred screen-selection preparation for the M2 original-scan reopen workflow; not complete M2 acceptance.
changes: Verified worker-private Float64 mesh-coordinate chunks can transfer without first materializing an ordinary numeric array in the decoder worker. Public project values remain ordinary arrays and other carriers retain their existing behavior.

Screen-selection preparation begins on a selection gesture instead of when brush mode is enabled, avoiding a full scan copy when history restores a selected mesh. GUI and MCP retain their existing selection operations.
diagnosis: An instrumented prior PLY-3 run started screen-selection-worker immediately after GUI Undo and allocated a 266108040-byte Float64 copy. The worker-start event and allocation did not occur at that point after deferring preparation. Browser, graphics, renderer and artifact allocations also contributed to the guarded peak; the trace does not establish a single cause of all prior failures.

reuseAudit.candidateOrigin: After successful project encoding, project-encoding-client remembers weak references to numeric arrays from the encoding snapshot. ProjectNumericReuse checks candidate values before returning one, but unpackProjectTransport can subsequently await another lookup after releasing an earlier candidate's transport buffer.
reuseAudit.publication: The decoding client caches display data before returning the session. Both GUI project open and MCP project import then await separate CAD restoration before publishing the restored session. A separate MCP-operation diagnostic mocked the decoded session and CAD import, deliberately mutated a decoded coordinate during CAD import, and observed the changed value published (999 instead of saved 1). This confirms the later publication gap under a synthetic mutation, but neither diagnostic demonstrates a supported editor operation mutating a candidate in either interval.
reuseAudit.workerScope: The production reuseNumericBuffer pack callback is used in the disposable decoding worker with cooperative:false. This is separate from main-thread numeric-array reuse and does not establish a production race during worker packing.
reuseAudit.constraints: Any candidate must preserve saved numeric values, aliases, existing direct decoder and display-cache behavior, cancellation and GUI/MCP parity. It must also pass the original PLY-3 workflow under the 4 GiB job limit; retaining all released buffers until publication can materially change that peak.
reuseAudit.revisionBoundary: ApplicationApi.currentRevision identifies geometry by positions identity, while MCP job checks compare revisions and GUI file opening uses the busy action lane. A focused synthetic test confirmed an in-place coordinate write does not change the revision, while replacing the array does. These mechanisms can detect ordinary state transitions but cannot by themselves prove a cooperatively hashed reused array remained unchanged. The test does not establish that a supported editor operation performs such an in-place write.
reuseAudit.freezeExperiment: A Node control froze one 33263505-element ordinary numeric array in 850.621 ms. Process heapUsed rose from 291179776 to 895527632 bytes across the freeze, and the guarded job peaked at 1174884352 bytes. A separate synthetic test confirmed that Object.freeze does not disable accessor setters. The encoder's reuse candidates also include normals, edges, and current/history/future geometry. This is not a browser or full-project result, but the measured allocation and changed object mutability make indiscriminate freezing unsuitable as an established fix under the narrow resource margin.
reuseAudit.witnessTiming: A synthetic Node test hashed 33263505 ordinary numeric values (266108040 encoded bytes) using the existing projectValueHash helper in 965.891 ms, matching an independent Node SHA-256. Its guarded process peak was 819118080 bytes and included an additional complete reference byte buffer. A separate isolated witness pass using per-element descriptor checks took 3449.407 ms and peaked at 848629760 bytes; it did not include that reference buffer. These tests measure individual hashes in Node, not browser responsiveness or full-workflow memory; repeated synchronous checks may visibly block the UI.
reuseAudit.isolatedPrototype: In a separate scratch copy, a test reproduced the display-cache ordering defect: synchronous publication could not see staged display data. The prototype now stages cache data before the publication callback, restores the prior cache on an exception, and preserves direct-decoder cache behavior through a separate deferred-publication mode. Fourteen focused decoder, publication, and mocked MCP tests passed under the guard. Subsequent adversarial tests demonstrated that a getter can mutate an already hashed element without changing the digest; rejecting accessor descriptors handles that example, but a Proxy descriptor trap and a reentrant check callback still bypassed the prototype. Another synthetic test demonstrated that a candidate changed during the initial value comparison could become its own incorrect fingerprint baseline. An isolated revision computes the baseline from the saved transport bytes instead and passed that test plus sixteen existing transport tests. These are synthetic inputs, not proven normal editor behavior. This candidate is not integrated and is not a complete safeguard; the Proxy and reentrant cases, browser responsiveness, real GUI/MCP restore after the latest revision, full-size memory and native acceptance remain unverified.
reuseAudit.replayInputs: The original PLY-3 input remains at C:/repo/alignment-example-files/ply-3.ply, 92765339 bytes, and its current SHA-256 matches bf738cb1da7aa2e2d26bc143c33e04313ad5096069d91cc22338cd0b01e9dcc2. reuseAudit.prototypePly3: A fresh isolated checkout at e10f32a8 with the witness prototype built successfully under the 4 GiB guard. An adapted diagnostic replay completed GUI Split and Extract, export and the full 475563378-byte MCP download. Its stream and independently checked disk SHA-256 both equal 965e3c730e785b35372f6dc1e905d8397db30e1a8189bb212269684b66a73ec2. GUI open reached the replacement confirmation, then session_get failed with BRIDGE_UNAVAILABLE before reopen geometry verification. The guard reported a 4058198016-byte peak and confirmed cleanup. A second instrumented replay again failed at the bridge, with 3858980864-byte peak and cleanup confirmed. The final four synchronous witness hashes occupied approximately 7.2 seconds; immediately afterward the bridge poll reported TimeoutError. A third diagnostic run changed the browser bridge request timeout from 10 to 30 seconds only in the isolated build: it remained connected and verified reopened geometry, but failed the final no-console-errors assertion on a script HTTP 404. Its 3964530688-byte peak stayed under the guard and cleanup was confirmed. A separate browser control reproduced the identical console message with the Vite-only build missing sw.js; generating the usual postbuild offline manifest changed the sw.js response from 404 to 200 and removed the error. The prior replay did not record the failing URL, so the control supports but does not directly prove its identity. A subsequent control with the manifest, the 30-second diagnostic timeout, and the saved-byte witness baseline passed GUI Split/Extract, complete MCP artifact download, reopen geometry, GUI post-reopen Undo/Redo and console checks. It peaked at 4108853248 bytes with cleanup confirmed. An additional candidate inserted task yields before final witness verification and GUI/MCP publication, restored the 10-second bridge timeout and passed 29 focused tests. Its original PLY-3 replay again failed with bridge poll TimeoutError immediately after a roughly 7.2-second final hash pass, at 4224843776-byte guarded peak with cleanup confirmed. Yielding between groups alone did not pass this replay. The known reentrant and Proxy cases also remain open.

validation.fullSuite: 50568 passed, 76 skipped; 4 GiB job guard passed and cleanup confirmed. An earlier run failed three gesture tests due to an optional viewport object-map lookup; the final source passed those focused tests and the full rerun.
validation.build: All 14 typecheck batches and the production build passed under the 4 GiB guard.
validation.selection: Thirty focused selection, gesture and MCP tests passed. A separate browser replay compared actual GUI gestures with public MCP for rectangle, circle, brush, freehand and line on point clouds and meshes, including subtraction and history.
validation.decoder: Thirteen private Float64 decoding tests cover carriers, aliases, signed zero, borrowed buffers and invalid input. A real browser decoder-worker check verified returned arrays, aliases, cancellation and worker termination.
validation.originalPly3: The exact final build ran GUI Split and Extract, public MCP artifact export and complete download, GUI in-place project reopen, geometry digests, and GUI Undo/Redo after reopen. Source, cutter and output geometry matched; input had 3691133 facets and output had 3695945 facets. The 4 GiB job guard passed at 4219797504 bytes with cleanup confirmed. An earlier untraced combined candidate passed at 4268969984 bytes; an instrumented run completed the workflow but exceeded the guard at 4297043968 bytes. These are separate runs and do not establish a general memory bound.
validation.combinedPreview: The two changes were applied to the existing combined preview without replacing other task work. Forty-six focused tests and a real decoder-worker browser check passed from that checkout. The original PLY-3 replay used the M2 candidate build, not the combined preview.
